title: mRemoteNG does not start PuTTY variants correctly
author: meyergru
body_snippet:
Version: Nightly Build — 20260318 (v1.82.0-beta.3)

It does not start PuTTY / KiTTY windows after being installed from the MSI package on my Windows 11 25H2 install.

A popup with an error message turns up:

`unknown option: "-hwndparent"`

I can start Putty from the settings menu to change settings.

When I choose the official Putty.exe path, it works.


It does not work for PuTTYNG.exe from the mRemoteNG directory with the above error.

For KiTTY (, the window is not opened within the mRemoteN...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Thanks for reporting @meyergru! 🙏

**Root cause:** The bundled `PuTTYNG.exe` (v0.83) has `InternalName="PuTTY"` with `"mRemoteNG"` in ProductVersion. The type detector matched this as "PuTTYNG" and passed `-hwndparent`, which this build doesn't support.

**Fix (commit `1137f7f`):** Tightened the PuTTYNG detection — now only matches when `InternalName` explicitly contains `"PuTTYNG"`. The bundled PuTTYNG 0.83 will be treated as regular PuTTY and use the `SetParent` window embedding method instead...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
@meyergru — additional fix for the busy-wait in `9ceaed4`! 🔧

**Root cause of CPU spike:** The `Resize` handler for embedded PuTTY (non-PuTTYNG) calls `MoveWindow()` which can trigger another `Resize` event recursively, creating an infinite loop that consumes 100% CPU on one core.

**Fix:** Added a reentrancy guard (`_isResizing` flag) that prevents recursive `MoveWindow` → `Resize` → `MoveWindow` loops.

Both fixes are now in the upcoming nightly:

Ah, well. It seems there is a conflict between this version of mRemoteNG and the old one. Once I rename the other program folder to mRemoteNG.bak, the crash disappears. Which is strange, considering the old one was in "C:\Programs (x86)\" and the other in "C:\Program Files\" and I started the correct instance from Explorer.

After reinitializing the settings, I still get the busy thread. This is independent of using extrnal PuTTY or disabling the specific path or using the app-delivered version ...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
@meyergru glad it's resolved! The assembly conflict with the old mRemoteNG folder makes sense — .NET probes for assemblies in adjacent directories. Renaming the old folder was the right fix.

Closing this one — both the `-hwndparent` fix and the busy-wait fix are in the latest nightly. Let us know if anything else comes up! 😊
